questions.q: The monthly sales of a product from January to April were 120, 135, 150 and 165 units, respectively. The cost price of the product was Rs. 240 per unit, and a fixed marked price was used for the product in all the four months. Discounts of 20%, 10% and 5% were given on the marked price per unit in January, February and March, respectively, while no discounts were given in April. If the total profit from January to April was Rs. 138825, then the marked price per unit, in rupees, was

Teams A, B, and C consist of five, eight, and ten members, respectively, such that every member within a team is equally productive. Working separately, teams A, B, and C can complete a certain job in 40 hours, 50 hours, and 4 hours, respectively. Two members from team A, three members from team B, and one member from team C together start the job, and the member from team C leaves after 23 hours. The number of additional member(s) from team B, that would be required to replace the member from team C, to finish the job in the next one hour, is
questions.solution: Work per single member per hour: A $=\frac{1}{5\times40}=\frac1{200}$, B $=\frac1{8\times50}=\frac1{400}$, C $=\frac1{10\times4}=\frac1{40}$. Starting team (2 A, 3 B, 1 C) works at $\frac{4+3+10}{400}=\frac{17}{400}$ per hour, so in 23 hours it finishes $\frac{391}{400}$ and $\frac{9}{400}$ is left. Once the C member goes, the 2 A and 3 B members give only $\frac{7}{400}$ per hour. The gap of $\frac{2}{400}$ needs two more B members, each adding $\frac1{400}$. **Answer: B (2)**

questions.q: In a school with 1500 students, each student chooses any one of the streams out of science, arts, and commerce, by paying a fee of Rs 1100, Rs 1000, and Rs 800, respectively. The total fee paid by all the students is Rs 15,50,000. If the number of science students is not more than the number of arts students, then the maximum possible number of science students in the school is
questions.solution: Let the students in science, arts and commerce be $s,a,c$ with $s+a+c=1500$. If everyone paid ₹1000 the total would be ₹15,00,000, so the actual extra of ₹50,000 gives $100s-200c=50000$, i.e. $s=500+2c$. Then $a=1500-s-c=1000-3c$. The condition $s\le a$ gives $500+2c\le1000-3c$, so $c\le100$. The largest $s$ is at $c=100$: $s=700$ (with $a=700$). **Answer: 700**

questions.q: In an arithmetic progression, if the sum of fourth, seventh and tenth terms is 99, and the sum of the first fourteen terms is 497, then the sum of first five terms is
questions.solution: The 4th, 7th and 10th terms are symmetric about the 7th, so their sum is $3t_7=99$ and $t_7=33$, i.e. $a+6d=33$. The sum of 14 terms is $7(2a+13d)=497$, so $2a+13d=71$. Substituting $a=33-6d$ gives $66+d=71$, so $d=5$ and $a=3$. Then $S_5=\frac52(2\cdot3+4\cdot5)=65$. **Answer: 65**

questions.q: Ankita walks from A to C through B, and runs back through the same route at a speed that is 40% more than her walking speed. She takes exactly 3 hours 30 minutes to walk from B to C as well as to run from B to A. The total time, in minutes, she would take to walk from A to B and run from B to C, is
questions.solution: Take walking speed $w$ and running speed $1.4w$. Walking B to C takes 210 minutes, so $BC=210w$. Running B to A also takes 210 minutes, so $AB=210\times1.4w=294w$. Walking A to B therefore takes 294 minutes, and running B to C takes $210w/1.4w=150$ minutes. Total $=294+150=444$ minutes. **Answer: 444**

questions.q: For a 4-digit number (greater than 1000), sum of the digits in the thousands, hundreds, and tens places is 15. Sum of the digits in the hundreds, tens, and units places is 16. Also, the digit in the tens place is 6 more than the digit in the units place. The difference between the largest and smallest possible value of the number is
questions.solution: Let the digits be $a,b,c,d$. The two sum conditions $a+b+c=15$ and $b+c+d=16$ differ by $d-a=1$. With $c=d+6$ we need $d\le3$, and $a=d-1\ge1$, so $d=2$ or $3$. For $d=2$: $a=1,c=8,b=6$, the number is 1682. For $d=3$: $a=2,c=9,b=4$, the number is 2493. Difference $=2493-1682=811$. **Answer: A (811)**

questions.q: Rahul starts on his journey at 5 pm at a constant speed so that he reaches his destination at 11 pm the same day. However, on his way, he stops for 20 minutes, and after that, increases his speed by 3 km per hour to reach on time. If he had stopped for 10 minutes more, he would have had to increase his speed by 5 km per hour to reach on time. His initial speed, in km per hour, was
questions.solution: The trip is 6 hours at speed $v$. Let $R$ be the distance still left when he stops. Reaching on time after a 20-minute halt means $\frac Rv=\frac R{v+3}+\frac13$, which simplifies to $R=\frac{v(v+3)}{9}$. With a 30-minute halt, $\frac Rv=\frac R{v+5}+\frac12$ gives $R=\frac{v(v+5)}{10}$. Equating, $10(v+3)=9(v+5)$, so $v=15$ km/h. **Answer: B (15)**

questions.q: The rate of water flow through three pipes A, B and C are in the ratio 4 : 9 : 36. An empty tank can be filled up completely by pipe A in 15 hours. If all the three pipes are used simultaneously to fill up this empty tank, the time, in minutes, required to fill up the entire tank completely is nearest to
questions.solution: Take the pipe rates as 4, 9 and 36 units per hour. Pipe A fills the tank in 15 hours, so the capacity is $4\times15=60$ units. All three together give 49 units per hour, so the time is $\frac{60}{49}$ hours $=\frac{3600}{49}\approx73.5$ minutes. The nearest option is 73. **Answer: A (73)**

questions.q: If $$f(x)= (x^{2} + 3x)(x^{2}+ 3x+2)$$ then the sum of all real roots of the equation $$\sqrt{f(x)+1}= 9701$$, is
questions.solution: Let $t=x^2+3x$. Then $f(x)=t(t+2)$ and $f(x)+1=(t+1)^2$, so the equation becomes $|t+1|=9701$. If $t=9700$, then $x^2+3x-9700=0$, whose discriminant $38809=197^2$ gives the real roots $97$ and $-100$, with sum $-3$. If $t=-9702$, then $x^2+3x+9702=0$ has a negative discriminant, so no real roots. The required sum is $-3$. **Answer: D (-3)**

questions.q: For real values of x, the range of the function $$f(x)=\dfrac{2x-3}{2x^{2}+4x-6}$$ is
questions.solution: Write $y=\frac{2x-3}{2x^2+4x-6}$ and clear the denominator: $2yx^2+(4y-2)x+(3-6y)=0$. For $y\neq0$ this quadratic needs a non-negative discriminant: $(4y-2)^2-8y(3-6y)=64y^2-40y+4=4(2y-1)(8y-1)\ge0$, so $y\le\frac18$ or $y\ge\frac12$. The value $y=0$ occurs at $x=\frac32$, and it already lies in $y\le\frac18$. The excluded points $x=1,-3$ cannot satisfy the equation because the numerator is non-zero there. **Answer: C**

questions.q: The sum of all the digits of the number $$(10^{50}+10^{25}-123)$$, is
questions.solution: $10^{25}-123$ is a 25-digit number made of twenty-two 9s followed by 877. In $10^{50}+10^{25}-123$ the 1 of $10^{25}$ is consumed by the borrow, so the number is a leading 1, then twenty-five zeros, then those 25 digits. Digit sum $=1+22\times9+(8+7+7)=1+198+22=221$. **Answer: B (221)**

questions.q: A triangle ABC is formed with AB = AC = 50 cm and BC = 80 cm. Then, the sum of the lengths, in cm, of all three altitudes of the triangle ABC is
questions.solution: The isosceles triangle has sides 50, 50, 80. The altitude from A to BC lands on the midpoint, so it is $\sqrt{50^2-40^2}=30$. Area $=\frac12\times80\times30=1200$. The altitude on each 50 cm side is $\frac{2\times1200}{50}=48$. Sum of altitudes $=30+48+48=126$. **Answer: 126**

questions.q: If $$\left( x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}} \right)=25$$ and $$x>0$$, then the value of $$\left( x^{7}+\frac{1}{x^{7}} \right)$$ is

In a class of 150 students, 75 students chose physics, 111 students chose mathematics and 40 students chose chemistry. All students chose at least one of the three subjects and at least one student chose all three subjects. The number of students who chose both physics and chemistry is equal to the number of students who chose both chemistry and mathematics, and this is half the number of students who chose both physics and mathematics. The maximum possible number of students who chose physics but not mathematics, is
questions.solution: Let $P\cap C=C\cap M=k$, $P\cap M=2k$ and the common region $=t$. Inclusion-exclusion: $75+111+40-(k+k+2k)+t=150$, so $t=4k-76$. Since $t\ge1$, we need $k\ge20$. Students with physics but not mathematics number $75-2k$ (the $2k$ already includes those taking all three), and this is largest at the smallest $k$. For $k=20$, $t=4$ and every region is non-negative, giving $75-40=35$. **Answer: B (35)**

questions.q: The sum of all possible real values of x for which $$\log_{x-3}{(x^{2}-9)}=\log_{x-3}{(x+1)}+2$$, is
questions.solution: A logarithm base $x-3$ must be positive and not 1, so $x>3$ and $x\ne4$. Moving terms, $\log_{x-3}\frac{x^2-9}{x+1}=2$, so $\frac{x^2-9}{x+1}=(x-3)^2$. Cancel $x-3$ (it is non-zero): $x+3=(x+1)(x-3)$, so $x^2-3x-6=0$ and $x=\frac{3\pm\sqrt{33}}2$. Only $\frac{3+\sqrt{33}}2\approx4.37$ is above 3 and not 4. The sum of valid values is just this root. **Answer: D**

questions.q: The average salary of 5 managers and 25 engineers in a company is 60000 rupees. If each of the managers received 20% salary increase while the salary of the engineers remained unchanged, the average salary of all 30 employees would have increased by 5%. The average salary, in rupees, of the engineers is
questions.solution: Original total salary $=30\times60000=₹18,00,000$. A 5% rise in the average means the total rises by $0.05\times1800000=₹90000$, and this is the 20% raise on the managers' pay. So managers earned $90000/0.2=₹4,50,000$ in all. Engineers earned $1800000-450000=₹13,50,000$, so their average is $1350000/25=₹54000$. **Answer: C (54000)**

questions.q: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB is parallel to DC, AD is perpendicular to AB, and AB = 3DC. If a circle inscribed in the trapezium touching all the sides has a radius of 3 cm , then the area, in sq. cm, of the trapezium is
questions.solution: Since $AD\perp AB$ and $AB\parallel DC$, the height $AD$ equals the diameter, 6. Let $DC=d$, so $AB=3d$. The slanting side is $BC=\sqrt{(3d-d)^2+6^2}=\sqrt{4d^2+36}$. For a quadrilateral with an incircle, $AB+DC=AD+BC$, so $4d-6=\sqrt{4d^2+36}$. Squaring gives $12d^2=48d$, so $d=4$. Area $=\frac12(12+4)\times6=48$. **Answer: A (48)**

questions.q: If $$12^{12x}\times 4^{24x+12}\times 5^{2y}=8^{4z}\times 20 ^{12x} \times 243^{3x-6}$$, where x , y and z are natural numbers, then $$ x + y + z $$ equals

In $$\triangle ABC$$, $$AB =AC= 12$$ cm and $$D$$ is a point on side $$BC$$ such that $$AD= 8$$ cm. If $$AD$$ is extended to a point $$E$$ such that $$\angle ACB = \angle AEB$$, then the length, in cm, of $$AE$$ is
questions.solution: Because $AB=AC$, $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$, and it is given that $\angle ACB=\angle AEB$. So in triangles $ABD$ and $AEB$, the angle at $A$ is common and $\angle ABD=\angle AEB$, which makes them similar. Hence $\frac{AB}{AE}=\frac{AD}{AB}$, i.e. $AB^2=AD\cdot AE$. Then $144=8\cdot AE$ and $AE=18$ cm. **Answer: C (18)**

questions.q: Vessels A and B contain 60 litres of alcohol and 60 litres of water, respectively. A certain volume is taken out from A and poured into B. After stirring, the same volume is taken out from B and poured into A. If the resultant ratio of alcohol and water in A is 15 : 4, then the volume, in litres, initially taken out from A is
questions.solution: After $x$ litres of alcohol go into B, B holds $60+x$ litres with $x$ alcohol and 60 water. The $x$ litres sent back carry water $\frac{60x}{60+x}$ and alcohol $\frac{x^2}{60+x}$. So A ends with water $\frac{60x}{60+x}$ and alcohol $(60-x)+\frac{x^2}{60+x}=\frac{3600}{60+x}$. Their ratio is $\frac{3600}{60x}=\frac{60}{x}$, and $\frac{60}{x}=\frac{15}{4}$ gives $x=16$ litres. **Answer: 16**

questions.q: The ratio of the number of coins in boxes A and B was 17:7. After 108 coins were shifted from box A to box B, this ratio became 37:20. The number of coins that needs to be shifted further from A to B, to make this ratio 1:1, is
questions.solution: Let the boxes hold $17k$ and $7k$ coins. After moving 108, $\frac{17k-108}{7k+108}=\frac{37}{20}$, so $340k-2160=259k+3996$, giving $81k=6156$ and $k=76$. Boxes now hold 1184 and 640 coins (ratio 1.85, as required). To equalise, each must hold $\frac{1824}{2}=912$, so A must give up $1184-912=272$ more. **Answer: 272**

questions.q: Let p, q and r be three natural numbers such that their sum is 900, and r is a perfect square whose value lies between 150 and 500. If p is not less than 0.3q and not more than 0.7q, then the sum of the maximum and minimum possible values of p is
questions.solution: Perfect squares strictly between 150 and 500 are $13^2=169$ up to $22^2=484$. For a given square $r$, let $s=p+q=900-r$. The conditions $p\ge0.3q$ and $p\le0.7q$ become $\frac{3s}{13}\le p\le\frac{7s}{17}$. The smallest $p$ comes from the smallest $s$, i.e. $r=484$, $s=416$: $p\ge96$. The largest $p$ comes from $r=169$, $s=731$: $p\le301$. Both bounds are whole numbers, so the sum is $96+301=397$. **Answer: 397**
